constitutional_basis: Article XXXIV — stop coding when reality is the next bottleneck (but the external solver IS the bottleneck, and we must choose HOW to acquire it)
Article XXXII — state strongest alternative (the current build route may not be the best)
EXPERIMENT_VALIDITY_GATE_V1 — infrastructure blocked is a legitimate state, but the blockage itself should be optimized
purpose: OpenFOAM-9 build has been stuck at 31% (1529/~4900 .o files) for multiple rounds. The build process repeatedly dies after ~30s. This is now a system-level risk. Rather than continuing to restart the same failing build (sunk-cost bias), Round 159 treats the environment acquisition as an experiment itself: compare multiple routes to a certified clotFoam environment and select the best.

the_target.what_we_need: A working clotFoam solver built on OpenFOAM v9 libraries
the_target.why_we_need_it: C5-X-R1 requires independent reproduction via clotFoam (Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion). Our internal World C flow simulator is custom Python; clotFoam is an external, widely-validated CFD solver. Without clotFoam, C5-X cannot be validated.
the_target.scientific_legitimacy: The external clotFoam project explicitly targets OpenFOAM v9 (per /home/z/clotFoam/README.md). The scientific target is legitimate.
the_target.current_route: Source build of OpenFOAM-9 from /home/z/OpenFOAM-9.tar.gz + MPICH from conda env 'sim' + system GCC. Build has been failing for 4+ rounds.

route_A_source_build_continuation.description: Continue the current route: build OpenFOAM-9 from source with MPICH + system GCC. Fix the build-dies-after-30s issue.
route_A_source_build_continuation.engineering_friction: HIGH (build keeps dying, root cause unknown — likely OOM killer or signal handling)
route_A_source_build_continuation.pros: Full source control; maximum independence; matches scientific target exactly
route_A_source_build_continuation.cons: Has been failing for 4 rounds; sunk-cost bias risk; root cause of build death unknown
route_A_source_build_continuation.diagnosis_of_failure: Build process receives SIGTERM or OOM kill after ~30s. Possible causes: (a) memory pressure (4GB system, build uses ~2GB), (b) setsid/nohup not properly detaching from parent shell, (c) bash subshell exiting on signal. Need to diagnose before continuing.

route_B_prebuilt_openfoam_docker.description: Use a prebuilt OpenFOAM v9 Docker image (e.g., opencfd/openfoam-default:9 or community images). Run clotFoam inside the container.
route_B_prebuilt_openfoam_docker.pros: High probability of success; fast; reproducible; Docker isolates dependencies
route_B_prebuilt_openfoam_docker.cons: Requires Docker installed (may not have it); slightly less independence than source build (but Docker images are open-source)
route_B_prebuilt_openfoam_docker.prerequisite_check_needed: Is Docker installed on this system?

route_C_conda_openfoam.description: Install OpenFOAM via conda-forge (openfoam-org channel or community builds).
route_C_conda_openfoam.engineering_friction: MEDIUM (conda packaging of OpenFOAM is less official)
route_C_conda_openfoam.pros: Fast if it works; integrates with existing conda env 'sim'
route_C_conda_openfoam.cons: OpenFOAM is not officially on conda-forge; community builds may be outdated or incomplete; clotFoam may not compile against conda OpenFOAM

route_D_system_package_apt.description: Install OpenFOAM via apt (Ubuntu/Debian package). The OpenFOAM Foundation provides apt repositories for v9.
route_D_system_package_apt.engineering_friction: LOW if sudo available, BLOCKED if not
route_D_system_package_apt.pros: Official route; fastest if sudo available; fully reproducible
route_D_system_package_apt.cons: Requires sudo (we don't have it); apt package may not match v9 exactly
route_D_system_package_apt.prerequisite_check_needed: Do we have sudo? (Earlier checks showed: NO — 'sudo: a password is required')

route_E_alternative_solver_substitution.description: If clotFoam cannot be acquired, use a DIFFERENT external CFD solver for independent reproduction. The constitutional requirement (Article XXVIII) is INDEPENDENT reproduction, not clotFoam specifically. Alternatives: SimVascular, ANSYS Fluent (if available), or a second independent OpenFOAM build.
route_E_alternative_solver_substitution.engineering_friction: MEDIUM (need to port clotFoam's physics to alternative solver)
route_E_alternative_solver_substitution.pros: Maintains independence requirement; avoids OpenFOAM build entirely
route_E_alternative_solver_substitution.cons: Requires porting clotFoam's platelet aggregation model to a different solver; may introduce new bugs; deviates from published clotFoam methodology

route_ranking.rank_1: Route D (apt) — score 0.285 — BUT BLOCKED on sudo
route_ranking.rank_2: Route C (conda) — score 0.128 — viable if conda package exists
route_ranking.rank_3: Route B (Docker) — score 0.090 — viable if Docker installed

route_ranking.recommendation: Try Route C (conda) first. If conda package doesn't exist or fails, try Route B (Docker). If Docker not available, try Route E (alternative solver). Route A (continue source build) is the WORST option — do not continue out of sunk-cost bias.
route_ranking.executive_decision: CEASE source build restarts. The current route has the lowest expected value. Investigate Routes C and B in Round 160.

sunk_cost_analysis.sunk_cost: ~4 rounds of build attempts, ~2 hours of coder time, ~1529 .o files compiled
sunk_cost_analysis.sunk_cost_fallacy: Continuing to restart the failing build because 'we've already invested so much' is the sunk-cost fallacy. The CEO Round 159 directive explicitly warns against this.
sunk_cost_analysis.rational_decision: The 1529 .o files are NOT wasted — they represent partial progress. But the BUILD PROCESS is broken. The rational decision is to abandon the build process (not the partial progress) and switch to a route with higher probability of success.
sunk_cost_analysis.what_to_preserve: The /home/z/OpenFOAM-9/ directory with 1529 .o files. If Route C or B succeeds, we may still use the partial build. If not, the partial build is harmless.
sunk_cost_analysis.what_to_abandon: The restart_openfoam_R157_v2.sh script and the persistent wrapper. These have failed repeatedly.

infrastructure_blocked_status.deadline_for_resolution: Round 162 (3 more rounds). If no route succeeds by Round 162, escalate to CEO for resource decision (e.g., HPC allocation, external collaboration).

honest_disclosure.what_this_analysis_does: Treats the environment acquisition as an experiment, not a sunk cost. Compares 5 routes on 4 dimensions. Identifies the current route as the WORST option.
honest_disclosure.what_this_analysis_does_NOT_do: Does not guarantee any route will succeed. Probability estimates are subjective (coder judgment, not calibrated). The actual success depends on system state we haven't verified (Docker installed? conda package exists?).
honest_disclosure.next_step: Round 160: (1) check if Docker is installed, (2) check if conda-forge has OpenFOAM v9, (3) if neither, attempt Route E (alternative solver). Route A (source build) is DEFERRED — only resume if all other routes fail AND the build-death root cause is diagnosed.
